# AP-INC-002 Operational Incident Response and Review

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This policy establishes the procedures for the reporting, coordination, and review of operational incidents at AeroPolicy Airport. It ensures that all incidents are managed in a timely and consistent manner to maintain safety, security, and operational efficiency. The policy applies to all incidents that occur on airport premises, including but not limited to those involving baggage, restricted items, ramp safety, and equipment. The procedures outlined in this policy are intended to support a structured response and continuous improvement through post-incident analysis.

Operational incidents may arise from a variety of sources, including human error, mechanical failure, or environmental conditions. These incidents can impact the safety of personnel, the security of the airport, or the integrity of airport operations. The response to such incidents must be coordinated across departments and roles to ensure that all affected areas are addressed. This policy defines the roles and responsibilities of key personnel in the incident response process and outlines the steps required to document and review each incident.

The scope of this policy includes all incidents that occur during the operation of the airport, regardless of the location or the type of activity. It does not cover incidents that are the subject of legal proceedings or those that fall under the jurisdiction of external regulatory bodies. The procedures outlined in this policy are designed to complement other airport policies and procedures, ensuring a comprehensive approach to incident management.

## 2. Incident Categories

Operational incidents are categorized into four main types: baggage, restricted-item, ramp safety, and equipment. Each category represents a distinct type of incident that requires specific handling and documentation. Baggage incidents involve the loss, delay, or mishandling of passenger luggage and are governed by the procedures outlined in AP-BAG-001. Restricted-item incidents involve the discovery or mishandling of items that are prohibited or restricted under airport security regulations and are addressed under AP-SEC-003. Ramp safety incidents involve any event that poses a risk to personnel or aircraft on the ramp area, including vehicle collisions, unauthorized access, or hazardous material spills. Equipment incidents involve malfunctions or failures of airport equipment, such as baggage carts, tow tractors, or communication systems.

Each incident must be reported immediately upon occurrence, regardless of its severity. The reporting process must ensure that all relevant details are captured, including the time, location, and nature of the incident. The categorization of an incident is essential for determining the appropriate response and for ensuring that the correct procedures are followed. The categorization also facilitates the tracking and analysis of incidents, enabling the airport to identify trends and implement preventive measures.

## 3. Reporting and First Response

All personnel who witness or are involved in an operational incident are required to report it immediately to their supervisor or the designated Reporting Staff Member. The Reporting Staff Member is responsible for ensuring that the incident is recorded in the airport's incident tracking system and that the appropriate personnel are notified. The first response to an incident should be focused on ensuring the safety of all individuals involved and minimizing any potential impact on airport operations.

In the case of a baggage incident, the Reporting Staff Member must follow the procedures outlined in AP-BAG-001 to ensure that the incident is properly documented and escalated. For restricted-item incidents, the Reporting Staff Member must refer to the procedures in AP-SEC-003 to ensure that the incident is handled in accordance with security protocols. The first response should also include an assessment of the incident's impact and the determination of whether additional resources or support are required.

## 4. Incident Coordinator Duties

The Incident Coordinator is responsible for overseeing the management of all operational incidents and ensuring that the response is coordinated and effective. The Incident Coordinator must open an incident record for every reported incident before the end of the shift in which it was reported. This record must include all relevant details, such as the time, location, and nature of the incident, as well as the actions taken during the initial response.

The Incident Coordinator is also responsible for assigning the appropriate personnel to manage the incident and for ensuring that all required documentation is completed. The Incident Coordinator must maintain communication with all relevant departments and personnel throughout the incident response process. This includes providing updates on the status of the incident and ensuring that all corrective actions are implemented in a timely manner.

## 5. Post-Incident Review

Following the resolution of an operational incident, a post-incident review must be conducted to determine the cause of the incident and to identify any corrective actions that can be implemented to prevent recurrence. This review is led by the Incident Coordinator and involves all relevant personnel, including the Airside Duty Manager and any affected departments. The review must include a detailed analysis of the incident, including the contributing factors and any procedural or systemic issues that may have contributed to the incident.

The post-incident review must result in a formal report that is documented in the airport's incident tracking system. This report must include the cause of the incident, the actions taken during the response, and the recommended corrective actions. The review must also include an assessment of the effectiveness of the initial response and any lessons learned from the incident. The findings and recommendations from the review must be shared with all relevant personnel and incorporated into the airport's operational procedures.

## 6. Records

All incident records must be maintained in the airport's incident tracking system and retained for a minimum of five years. These records must include the incident report, the incident record opened by the Incident Coordinator, and the post-incident review report. The records must be accessible to authorized personnel for audit or review purposes. All incident records must be reviewed annually to ensure their accuracy and completeness. The records must also be updated as necessary to reflect any changes in procedures or incident management practices.
